title: PR regression custodian: adaptive load-safeguard for tokens/sec and p95
creator: Ayesha Patel
description:
Problem: We still see noisy CI windows and occasional latent regressions slipping into main because single-run token/sec and p95 snapshots are sensitive to microbursts and cache-warm variability. Goal: Build a PR-side "custodian" that normalizes signal across commit candidates, runs a lightweight canonical replay, and produces a statistically grounded gate decision (block/allow) for tokens/sec and p95.

Scope & deliverables:
- A CI job definition that runs on every PR and compares candidate vs rolling canonical workload (same model, sequence mix, hardware profile).
- Synthetic workload generator with jittered sequence lengths, KV cache priming, and warmup cycles to reduce cold-start variance.
- Aggregation layer that computes tokens/sec (aggregate) and latency p95 with bootstrap confidence intervals.
- Decision rule: bootstrap-based nonparametric test with adjustable thresholds (default: block on >=5% p95 increase OR >=7% tokens/sec drop with p<=0.01 after multiple-test correction).
- Golden replay fallback: if gate trips, schedule full replay on dedicated infra and attach grafana traces + example traces to the PR.
- Telemetry: dashboard tile and PR comment summary with CI artifact links.

Non-goals: replacing long-running nightly baselining or benchmarking clusters used by perf team. This is a fast pre-merge guard to catch high-confidence regressions.
acceptance_criteria: CI job runs for PRs and completes within target budget (<=20m wall time) on typical diff sizes
Signals produced: tokens/sec and p95 with 95% CI and per-slice breakdown (seq len buckets, cache-warm state)
Decision reproducible: repeated runs on same candidate produce same pass/fail in >=95% of trials in internal tests
When gate trips, PR receives an automated comment with failing metrics, grafana link, and a link to the scheduled golden replay
True positive rate >= 90% on the curated regression corpus and false positive rate <= 2% on synthetic noise corpus
comments: 2026-02-16 - Ayesha: Kickoff meeting with perf/ci/infra. Agreed to reuse existing runner images and add a 'custodian' step that orchestrates 3 warmup runs + 5 measurement runs.

2026-02-20 - Diego: PoC generator implemented (repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ci-tools/tree/eng/ci-custodian). Initial microbench on t4 shows 8-12% variance on p95 without warmup; warmup reduces to ~3%.

2026-02-24 - Diego: Chosen statistical approach: percentile bootstrap on paired samples with Holm-Bonferroni adjustment across metrics and slices. Documented rationale in design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/Perf+Custodian+Design

2026-03-02 - Review notes from Perf team (Lina Zhang): prefer hierarchical pooling across similar hardware groups to increase sensitivity for small diffs. We'll add pooling as opt-in parameter for project-level configs.
2026-03-05 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference-runtime/pull/2891 (adds ci job definition + synthetic workload generator). Requesting review from @perf-team and @ci-ops.
2026-03-08 - CI-ops (Samir): flagged runner resource budget; suggested limit of 4 concurrent custodian jobs per runner pool, and a max of 2x default GPU allocation for golden replays.
2026-03-09 - Diego: Added grafana panel and PR summary template. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/ci-perf/pr-custodian. Added PR bot comment example that shows metrics and failure reasons.

2026-03-10 - Ayesha: Decision to ship alpha behind feature flag 'pr_custodian_alpha' and enable for runtime-2.4 related PRs only. Plan: run alpha for 2 weeks, collect FP/TP metrics, then widen rollout. Noted follow-up on automating golden replay triage.
